title: Evidence Post-Processing & Routing Playbook
body:
Purpose
This playbook describes the post-processing and routing layer for control evidence produced by collectors and harvesters. It focuses on responsibilities that live downstream of raw ingestion: normalization, enrichment, canonical audit mapping, retention/tombstoning, SIEM export formatting, and RBAC-aware access tagging. The goal is to define operational contracts, transformation rules, failure modes, testing steps, and rollout guidance for the post-processor service ("evidence-postproc") so teams can reliably use automated evidence for audits and incident response.

Scope and assumptions
- Inputs: events emitted by collectors/harvesters (S3 batches, push webhooks, streaming events). Formats vary: JSONL, compressed protobuf, CSV exported from legacy tools.
- Outputs: normalized evidence artifacts stored in Evidence Store, SIEM-compatible event feeds (Elastic/QRadar/Datadog), and an index used by control-evidence UIs and SRM workflows.
- This doc intentionally excludes collector attachment-level parsing (e.g., raw disk forensics); it focuses on the canonicalization and routing layer after the collector produces an initial event.
- Assumes RBAC v2 role tagging is already attached to the original request context where available; postproc must preserve and augment role-based metadata.

High-level architecture
1) Ingest endpoint(s): the post-processor subscribes to a validated topic (Kafka: evidence-ingest-validated) and an s3-batch queue for large payloads.
2) Normalizer: classifies event type, extracts canonical fields (actor, actor_type, action, resource, resource_type, timestamp, request_id, region, environment, collector_id).
3) Enricher: performs lookups (user directory, API key to customer mapping, model pin -> model-family mapping), attaches TTL/retention class and sensitivity tags.
4) Canonical audit mapper: maps events into the audit schema used for controls (control_id, control_category, control_evidence_type, severity_score, actionable_flag). Mapping must be reversible so we can point back to raw input.
5) Exporter/routing: based on routing policy (SLO strictness, sensitivity, region), fork outputs to: Evidence Store (immutable object), SIEM export pipeline, real-time alerting bus, and compliance-index DB.
6) Observability & tracing: every event must carry trace_id and processing stage timestamps. Failures create an evidence-processing-failure record written to dead-letter stream and alerted.

Canonical field set (required)
- event_id (string)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- request_id (string)
- collector_id (string)
- actor_id (string) or null
- actor_type (user|service|key|unknown)
- action (string) e.g., "secret.create", "model.deploy"
- resource_id (string)
- resource_type (string) e.g., "model", "deployment", "key"
- outcome (success|failure|unknown)
- raw_payload_ref (s3:// or gs://)
- sensitivity_tag (public|internal|confidential|restricted)
- rbac_tags (list) — roles/groups from RBAC v2 attached to the action
- control_mappings (list) — control ids assigned during canonical mapping

Transformation rules and examples
- Timestamp normalization: accept epoch, RFC3339 variants; normalize to UTC ISO8601 with millisecond precision. Missing timestamps => use collector_received_time but flag as imputed.
- Actor resolution: if actor_id is missing but api_key present, resolve api_key -> owner and set actor_type=key; attach api_key_fingerprint. If unable to resolve, set actor_type=unknown and add lookup_failure=true.
- Resource canonicalization: map multiple resource identifiers to a single canonical id using model-registry API for model artifacts and deployment-registry for runtime objects. Failures should not block export; mark as lookup_failed.
- PII redaction: any string fields matching PII regex (emails, SSN patterns) must be redacted from exported SIEM payloads; keep original in Evidence Store but mark redaction applied.

SIEM export profiles
We support three SIEM profiles tailored to customer needs. Each profile is produced by the exporter and serialized into the target connector.
- event-minimal (for high-volume telemetry): includes event_id, timestamp_utc, action, resource_type, outcome, sensitivity_tag, control_mappings, rbac_tags. PII redacted.
- event-rich (default): everything in event-minimal plus actor_id (hashed), resource_id (hashed for restricted), request_id, collector_id, severity_score, indicators (if any).
- forensic (for incident response): unredacted fields retained but encrypted with per-tenant CEK before SIEM export and access controlled via KMS; separate export channel and strict retention.

Routing policy matrix (simplified)
- If sensitivity_tag == restricted => Evidence Store + Forensic export channel (no event-minimal exports).
- If control_mappings includes high-importance controls (list maintained in Confluence) => duplicate to realtime-alerts bus and to SIEM event-rich.
- Low sensitivity and high-volume events => event-minimal to SIEM; keep full object in Evidence Store for 90 days by default.

RBAC v2 integration notes
- Postproc must not attempt to authorize access; it only annotates artifacts with rbac_tags pulled from incoming context or via lookup. The access control decision is enforced at the Evidence Store and Console layers using RBAC v2 policies.
- rbac_tags format: role:<role_name>, org:<org_id>, team:<team_id>. Use string list.
- Ensure tags are preserved through any transformation and added to SIEM payloads where allowed. If sensitive roles are detected (e.g., admin), add sensitive_flag=true to outbound routing decisions.

Chain-of-custody and evidence immutability
- Every evidence artifact written to Evidence Store must include provenance: source_collector, ingress_time, processing_trace_id, processor_version, and content_hash (SHA256).
- Postproc must compute and persist a signed manifest (manifest is a JSONL line stored alongside the artifact) signed using service signing key rotated monthly. Manifests are required for audits and must be exportable to auditors in CSV/JSON form.

Error handling and DLQ behavior
- Transient failures (3xx/5xx from lookups): retry with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts. If still failing, mark lookup_failed and continue (non-blocking).
- Validation failures (missing required canonical fields): write to evidence-dlq with schema_error and alert SRE pager for >100/day.
- Export failures (downstream SIEM connector outage): buffer events in local durable queue (S3-backed) with 7-day TTL and continue to write to Evidence Store. Emit metric siem.export.down and escalate with repeating alerts.

Operational runbook (high level)
1) On alert "evidence-processor-high-schema-errors": run data quality query against canonicalization metrics; sample 50 dlq entries and inspect collector_id and schema difference.
2) On "siem-export-failure": verify connector health, check connector auth tokens, promote emergency bypass to send event-minimal to alternate SIEM if configured.
3) On "provenance-mismatch": run manifest verification job (monthly); if mismatch > 0.1% of checks, pause ingestion for collector, notify collector owner.

Test plan and rollout strategy
- Unit tests: canonicalizer mapping table coverage, TTL classification, PII redaction unit tests.
- Integration tests: end-to-end pipeline from test-collector to Evidence Store and SIEM staging. Include fault-injection for enrichment lookup failures.
- Canary rollout: enable postproc for 5% of traffic per collector (per-collector gating), monitor dlq rate, processing latency p50/p95, and false-positive control mappings.
- Post-rollout: run an audit sample comparing 500 post-processed artifacts vs raw inputs and verify reversible mapping.

Open questions / design trade-offs
- Should the post-processor perform RBAC lookup for missing context, or should that be deferred to the Evidence Store? Current recommendation: annotate but do not authorize.
- Encryption-for-export vs store-level side encryption: customers request per-tenant encrypted SIEM exports; this requires connector changes and KMS integration per tenant.
- Retention classes: propose 4 default classes but customers needed custom class mapping in contracts.

References and related docs
- Evidence retention policy (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- Collector contracts and plugin spec (see code repo pull request).
- RBAC v2 spec (internal Confluence).

Appendix: quick examples
1) Example input (collector JSON snippet): {
  "collected_at": 1676100000,
  "collector_id": "k8s-audit-v2",
  "payload": {"verb": "patch", "resource": "/models/mdl-123", "user": "alice@corp"},
  "request_id": "req-22ab"
}

2) Example canonical output (abbreviated): {
  "event_id": "evt-0001",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-02-10T15:20:35.123Z",
  "collector_id": "k8s-audit-v2",
  "actor_id": "alice@corp",
  "action": "model.patch",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "mdl-123",
  "sensitivity_tag": "internal",
  "control_mappings": ["CTRL-5.2"]
}

Contact

Status notes
This is an operational draft intended for review by collector owners, SRE, and privacy. After review we will convert mappings to a canonical table and publish as a companion CSV in the code repo.
